# Mikhail Simakhov

> Mike is a student who builds AI agent systems and small experiments on how language models are tested. Since 1 September 2026 he has studied A-levels in Computer Science, Physics and Maths in Cambridge, UK, on an academic scholarship.

Mike is interested in how people actually use AI, and how you test what a model can really do. Mike builds with Claude Code, an AI coding tool, and it writes the code at his direction. One of Mike's papers is under review at a peer-reviewed conference, and the other is an unreviewed draft.

## New

- [Open Door](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/opendoor): public repo. Open Door was built solo at the {Tech: Europe} Agentic AI Hack in London on 19 Sep 2026. It is an agent that reads London GP registration pages and flags the ones asking new patients for documents nhs.uk says are not needed. All verdicts are AI readings of website wording, with no human review. On 28 Sep 2026 the organisers wrote that Open Door took first place in the Pydantic side challenge (not the main track).
- [Photo-to-Physics](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/pixel-perfect-replica): public repo. Built at the GPT-6 Astra Hackathon in London on 6 Oct 2026 with GPT-6 Astra, Codex and Lovable. A student photographs a physics problem or describes an experiment, the model writes a browser experiment, and deterministic code checks it against the textbook formula, with up to three correction rounds. Three topics only.
- [Nyx](https://editor.joinarcade.ai/play/e2b6663e-4f68-4710-853f-6ca90dd37c96): published on Arcade. Built at the Cambridge x Arcade AI Hackathon, West Hub, Cambridge, on 3 to 4 Oct 2026, in the Arcade Track. A physics sandbox game for ages 7 to 17: players take short classes on gravity and time with a teacher character, predict, run the experiment, pass a three-question check and unlock powers. Anything that bends real physics is labelled GAME RULE. Every script and asset was generated by Arcade's Morph agents from his prompts.
- [Rental Housing Law Navigator](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/rental-housing-law-navigator): public repo. Submitted to Hack-Nation x RealPage, an online hackathon, on 4 Oct 2026. A user types a US address and a date and sees which rental housing rules apply; each rule check ends as yes, no or unknown with the source sentence quoted word for word. 3 states, 10 cities, 6 rule categories, 500 sample addresses. 30.9 percent of results are unknown; no human or lawyer reviewed it; not legal advice.
- [Skopos](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/skopos-demo): public repo. Skopos is a one-day hackathon prototype built with a team at Worlds London on 12 Sep 2026. It is a readiness check for home robots. There is no robot, no physics and no trained policy, the metrics are labelled placeholder, and the room map is plausible, not measured.
- [Shutdown-framing](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/shutdown-framing): research, public repo. A dependency-free Python harness for shutdown-resistance experiments on language models comes with a three-part pre-flight screen that includes a comprehension check, a behavioural floor and a custodial control to say whether a model can give a readable result at all. Seven small open models from six lineages ran locally on his laptop (as of 2 Oct 2026). None passed the whole screen, so no framing effect is claimed.
- [Chalk Talk](https://github.com/msimakhov-star/chalk-talk): public repo, work in progress started 22 Oct 2026 for the Amazon Developer Hackathon. Only the architecture contracts and a scaffold exist so far.
- AI society: Mike founded an AI society at his college in Cambridge. The first session ran on 24 Sep 2026 and it meets weekly on Thursdays.
- Talk: on 21 Oct 2026 Mike agreed to give a 20-minute talk at AI Meetup Cambridge in January 2027 about agentic workflows and the always-on agent system that runs his week. The exact date is not fixed yet.
- IFoRE 2026 (Sigma Xi): abstract submitted 4 Sep 2026 and accepted on 7 Oct 2026; Mike decided not to register, so he did not present.

## Papers

- A pre-flight screen for shutdown-resistance evaluations (under review at a peer-reviewed ML conference, decision December 2026): The paper proposes a three-part check to run before a shutdown-resistance experiment, made of a comprehension check, a behavioural floor and a custodial control. It was tested on six small open models from five model families, run locally, with 4,800 trials and 594 comprehension probes. No model passed the whole screen, so the thresholds are not calibrated yet. The paper does not claim a framing effect in either direction. The starting idea is Mike's. AI assistants proposed the testable design, the thresholds and the three-part screen, AI coding tools wrote and ran the harness and did the analysis, and an AI language model drafted the text.
- Manipulation-Check Reporting in LLM Shutdown-Resistance Evaluations: A Systematic Review (draft): This draft reviews 19 publicly posted shutdown-resistance evaluations of language models from January 2023 to August 2026. None of the 19 reports a formal comprehension check, and none reports a null result. The coding was done by AI language models and has not been checked by a person yet, and the text was drafted by an AI language model. The work is not submitted and not published.

## Experiments (local, no public repo)

- JudgeCheck: JudgeCheck is a single-file Python harness that uses only the standard library. It asks a judge model to compare every answer pair twice, with A and B swapped, to measure position, length and label effects when an LLM is used as a judge. It was a small pilot on 7 local models. Self-preference is not measured.
- RU-EN Drift: Small local models graded 60 synthetic, AI-generated Russian essays under English instructions and under Russian instructions. Adding a confident or an uncertain sentence to an essay lowered its score. There was no consistent language effect. The language and framing interaction he first expected did not replicate and was retracted. In October 2026 the setup was rerun on PolyMath, a public parallel English and Russian set of 125 maths items: of qwen2.5:3b's 25 apparent English-only wins only 6 survived three controls (answer extraction, translation errors in the item set, rewording); gemma3:4b showed no significant gap. One run at temperature 0, reworded items not checked by a native speaker.
- Turns: Turns is a single-file browser grid puzzle made as a one-day prototype.
- PromptCloak: PromptCloak is a single-file offline browser tool that swaps private details in a prompt for placeholders. Its detection is heuristic, so it can miss things.

## Tools

- [Horizon](https://msimakhov-star.github.io/projects/#tools): an always-on autonomous agent driven over Telegram in Russian or English. It plans a task, a council of AI reviewers votes on the plan, a specialist agent does the work, and it reports back. Python, Claude CLI, Telegram Bot API, Linux server.
- [Case Dojo](https://msimakhov-star.github.io/projects/#tools): an offline-first web app for studying business thinking, with spaced repetition, worked cases, and an optional AI coach. React, Vite, Express, Claude API.
- [Summer Calendar](https://msimakhov-star.github.io/projects/#tools): the tracker web app for his summer 2026 plan, backed by plain JSON files in git. Python, vanilla JS.
